name: thanos_receive_http_request_latency_high
title: Thanos Receive Http Request Latency High
description: Thanos Receive has a 99th percentile latency seconds for requests.

source.upstream_alert: Thanos Receive Http Request Latency High
source.upstream_query: (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (job, le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~".*thanos-receive.*", handler="receive"}[5m]))) > 10 and sum by (job) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~".*thanos-receive.*", handler="receive"}[5m])) > 0)
source.upstream_description: Thanos Receive {{$labels.job}} has a 99th percentile latency of {{ $value }} seconds for requests.
source.query_normalized: The upstream threshold could not be lifted out of the expression (its outermost operator is and/or/unless, or it compares against another series), so the expression is normalised to 1 per matching series and the alert fires on any match. The observed value in the notification is therefore always 1.

query_condition.promql: ((histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (job, le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~".*thanos-receive.*", handler="receive"}[5m]))) > 10 and sum by (job) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~".*thanos-receive.*", handler="receive"}[5m])) > 0)) * 0 + 1

notes: 10s threshold is a rough default; ingestion latency scales with your sample throughput — adjust based on your baseline.
